literal: He hoarded abundant great wealth; he who does not enjoy that is a dead man; there is nothing remaining for him to do.
translation: He who hoards vast, abundant wealth but does not enjoy it is as good as dead; there is nothing else left for him to do.
modern: எல்லையைக் கடந்த பெரும் செல்வத்தைச் சேர்த்து வைத்து, அதனை அனுபவிக்காமல் வாழ்கின்றவன் இறந்தவனுக்கு ஒப்பாவான்; அவனால் செய்யக்கூடிய பயன் வேறு ஒன்றும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute uselessness of hoarded wealth that is never put to use. The phrase 'வாய் சான்ற பெரும்பொருள்' describes a massive fortune that exceeds all normal limits. The poet argues that a person who hoards such wealth but does not consume or enjoy it ('அஃதுண்ணான்') is functionally equivalent to a dead person ('செத்தான்'). Just as a corpse cannot utilize worldly goods, the miser derives no benefit from his riches, leaving him with no active purpose or utility ('செயக்கிடந்தது இல்') in life.
